name: Enjin CryptoItems ERC-1538 registry adapter initialize manager takeover
summary: The two Enjin ERC-1538 adapter registries route every registered adapter selector through their own fallback, including the adapter template's initialize(uint256). Called directly on a registry, that initializer runs in registry storage, where its once-only guard slot was never set and its owner slot is the registry's pending-manager slot. Any caller could therefore make itself pending manager and accept management. The attacker took over both registries and pointed the item-adapter transfer selectors at its own code. It then pulled ERC-1155 items from holders without approval and melted them, draining 6.58M ENJ of backing from the platform reserve.

loss.notes: Gross reserve depletion across 595 attacker transactions (blocks 25834071-25834993). Stolen items were melted for 6,518,518.5545533333333333 ENJ paid to the attack contract, plus 61,108.67468 ENJ the reserve paid to 22 other recipients inside the same melt calls (not deducted). The anchor transaction alone melted 5,231,353 ENJ to the attacker. Value of stolen items that were not melted is not measured. The attacker's later ENJ swaps do not set the valuation.

ageReset.description: The manager's updateContract call emitted FunctionUpdate(bytes4,address,address,string) for selector 0xfe4b84df (initialize(uint256)). It routed that selector on registry A from 0x0 to the ERC-721 adapter template 0x24591e79, making the unguarded initializer reachable in registry storage. It is the only pre-exploit FunctionUpdate for that selector; the registry runtime (block 13530687) and the template (block 13530845) are older.

FunctionUpdate for selector 0xfe4b84df (initialize(uint256)) routed that selector on registry B from 0x0 to the ERC-20 adapter template 0x75512f84. It is the only pre-exploit FunctionUpdate for that selector; the registry runtime (block 13530678) and the template (block 13530836) are older.

limitations: Sibling registry exploited in the same anchor transaction; its initialize route was installed at block 13530886, two blocks before target-1's (13530888), so target-1 carries the knot.

sources.note: Reviewed root cause, admission and first exercise. Registries, templates and the attack contract are unverified on Etherscan, so behavior comes from traces and a fork. debug_traceTransaction(callTracer) of source-1 (block 25834071, tx 1): attacker EOA 0x5ec1ba78 calls attack contract 0x7083ddec (created in tx 0 of the same block, 0x2fd2c517b3456adccbcd57528c8ef04d382d49be1611a146aee6d9784043cc14, whose creation trace touches no registry). The attack contract calls registry A 0x13fa4b9a with initialize(1) (0xfe4b84df), delegatecalled into 0x24591e79, then acceptManager() (0x48ff15b3, native), then updateContract (0x61455567, delegatecall to 0x04866013). It does the same on registry B 0x268c039a, where initialize delegatecalls into 0x75512f84. Receipt logs 0 and 3 are ManagerUpdate(address,address) (0xbe4cc281) from 0x1952e45d to 0x7083ddec. Logs 1 and 4 are FunctionUpdate routing stealNFT(address,address,uint256) (A) and transferFrom (B) to attacker-created 0x99294e5e, then initialize and acceptManager to attacker stubs 0x73497e1c and 0x6561d8a6. Item clones (for example 0xa1addf20 and 0xff1727d2) call registry.delegates(bytes4) (0xa0a2daf0) and delegatecall 0x99294e5e. That body calls platform 0xfaafdc07 selectors 0x41c1df0e and 0xf95d7da3, which move holders' items without owner approval, and the stolen items are then melted through the platform. Mechanism, reproduced on an anvil fork of block 25834070: registry A slots 0/1/2 are 0x1952e45d (manager), 0xe5cb0c8e (pending manager set by transferManager tx 0x524b0324949e79740d6ee8d8fb146e14fb8b2c99203c209f1b3721b203b6223c, never accepted) and 0. initialize(1) from arbitrary 0x...beef succeeds with slot1=0xbeef and slot2=1. acceptManager() from 0xbeef then emits ManagerUpdate and sets slot0=0xbeef. A second initialize from another address reverts (guard slot2!=0). prestateTracer diffMode on source-1 shows the same slot0/slot2 writes on both registries. The defect is victim code: the template's once-only initializer is reachable through the registry fallback in registry storage, and the manager key was not used. Attacker-installed bodies are attack machinery. First exercise: pre-state slot1 equals the transferManager value and slot2=0 on both registries at block 25834070, so no successful initialize (which writes both slots) preceded source-1. Etherscan txlist for each registry shows only deployment, updateContract and transferManager by 0x1952e45d before source-1. eth_getLogs ManagerUpdate on both registries from deployment to 25834070 returns none.

Reviewed age history. Runtime keccak: registry A 0xe6e38940...fab2, empty at 13530686, same at 13530687 (deployment tx idx 78, top-level CREATE by 0x1952e45d) and at 25834070. Registry B 0xbdab4fc2...07ca, empty at 13530677, same at 13530678 (tx idx 6) and at 25834070. Template 0x24591e79 0xfd85334a...84ce, empty at 13530844, same at 13530845 and 25834070. Template 0x75512f84 0x8c07911c...efa9, empty at 13530835, same at 13530836 and 25834070. eth_call delegates(0xfe4b84df) on A returns 0x0 at 13530887 and 0x24591e79 at 13530888 and 25834070. On B it returns 0x0 at 13530885 and 0x75512f84 at 13530886 and 25834070. eth_getLogs on each registry from its deployment block to 25834070: A emits FunctionUpdate (0x3234040c) once at 13530687 (updateContract to 0x04866013) and 17 times in source-7 (logs 17-33, ERC-721 template selectors; log 33 topic1 0xfe4b84df, topic3 0x24591e79), plus CommitMessage. B emits FunctionUpdate once at 13530678 and 11 times in source-8 (logs 70-80; log 80 topic1 0xfe4b84df, topic3 0x75512f84). Neither emits any further log before source-1, so the initialize route and the registry runtime persisted unchanged. The module route is the latest change that made the vulnerable combination reachable, so ages run from source-7 (target-1, 151917396 s) and source-8 (target-2, 151917445 s).

Reviewed gross loss. Etherscan tokentx for ENJ 0xf629cbd9 and reserve 0x4e643a25 from block 25834000 lists 832 transfers. Every reserve outflow is in a successful transaction sent by the attacker EOA to 0x7083ddec (Etherscan txlist: 606 successful calls; 595 of them carry reserve outflows, from source-1 at block 25834071 to source-11 at block 25834993, timestamp 1787694395). Totals: 6579627229233333333333300 wei out, of which 6518518554553333333333300 goes to 0x7083ddec (forwarded in full to the EOA) and 61108674680000000000000 goes to 22 other recipients inside the same melt calls (largest EOA 0x862e4dc5, 36236 ENJ). There are no reserve inflows. Cross-check: reserve balanceOf is 9852235680834846022159376 at 25834070 and 3272608451601512688826076 at 25834993 and 25835100, a difference equal to the outflow total. In source-1 alone the reserve pays 5231353 ENJ to the attack contract and 7000 ENJ to 0x862e4dc5.
